n: Jacob continues with Isaiah 51. To those who seek righteousness, the Lord says: remember where you came from — the “rock” and “quarry” you were cut from.

f.w: the rock from whence ye are hewn
f.g: Your origin — explained in the next verse as Abraham and Sarah.

n: Abraham and Sarah are Israel’s ancestors. God called Abraham alone and blessed him with countless descendants, so He can surely restore Israel now.
The Lord will comfort Zion and turn her ruins into a garden like Eden, full of joy, thanks, and music.
God calls His people to listen: His law and justice will go out as a light to all people.
His righteousness and salvation are near. His “arm” — His power — will judge, and distant lands will trust in it.

f.g: God’s power to act and save.

n: Heaven and earth will pass away like smoke and wear out like a garment, but God’s salvation lasts forever.

f.w: the heavens shall vanish away like smoke

n: To those with God’s law written on their hearts: don’t fear people’s scorn or insults.

f.w: in whose heart I have written my law

n: Scoffers will be eaten away like wool by moths, but God’s righteousness endures through all generations.

f.w: the moth shall eat them up

n: The people cry for God to awake and act as in ancient times. Rahab and the dragon are poetic images of chaos-monsters, here standing for Egypt, which God defeated at the Exodus.

f.g: A poetic name for a sea monster, used for Egypt.
Another chaos-monster image, also used of Pharaoh.

n: God dried the sea and made a path for the redeemed to cross — the Red Sea crossing.

f.w: made the depths of the sea a way for the ransomed to pass over

n: So the Lord’s redeemed will return to Zion with singing. The Book of Mormon adds “holiness” to the everlasting joy upon their heads. Sorrow will flee away.

f.w: the redeemed of the Lord shall return

n: God says, “I am he that comforteth you.” Why fear mortal men who wither like grass?

f.w: I am he that comforteth you

n: Why forget your Maker and live in constant fear of oppressors? Where is their fury now? It will vanish before God.
The captive in exile will soon be released, not left to die in a pit or go hungry.
“I am the Lord thy God, whose waves roared; the Lord of Hosts is my name.” The Book of Mormon omits the KJV phrase “that divided the sea.”

f.g: The Lord of the armies of heaven.

n: God has put His words in His people’s mouths and sheltered them in His hand, establishing them as His people.

f.w: I have put my words in thy mouth

n: Jerusalem is called to wake up. She has drunk the cup of God’s wrath down to the bitter dregs — a picture of the suffering that followed her sins.

f.g: The bitter sediment at the bottom of a cup.

n: None of Jerusalem’s children are left to guide her or take her hand.

Two “sons” come to her in her ruin. The KJV reads “two things” (desolation and destruction); the Book of Mormon’s “two sons” is often connected by Latter-day Saints to the two prophets of Revelation 11, who minister in Jerusalem in the last days.
Her other sons have fainted in the streets, caught like a wild antelope in a net, overwhelmed by God’s rebuke. The Book of Mormon adds “save these two.”

f.g: Hebrew te’o — likely an antelope or oryx.

n: Hear this, you who are afflicted and staggering — though not from wine.
The Lord pleads His people’s cause: He takes the cup of trembling from their hand. They will never drink it again.

f.w: pleadeth the cause of his people

n: Instead, He gives the cup to their oppressors, who had forced Israel to lie down like a road for them to walk on.

f.w: Bow down, that we may go over
f.g: Conquerors sometimes literally walked on the backs of the defeated.

n: Now Jacob quotes Isaiah 52:1. Zion is called to awake and put on her strength and beautiful garments; nothing unclean will enter her again. Latter-day revelation explains this strength as priesthood authority.

f.w: put on thy strength, O Zion

n: Isaiah 52:2: Jerusalem must shake off the dust, rise, and free herself from the chains on her neck. Latter-day revelation explains these chains as the curses of God, which scattered Israel can shake off by returning to Him.

f.w: loose thyself from the bands of thy neck
